claim: A service owner offers a service through PrivateLink by putting a Network Load Balancer in front of it and creating a PrivateLink service registered with that load balancer; a consumer creates an interface VPC endpoint, which appears as network interfaces with private IPs in the consumer VPC.
question: What does each side create to use AWS PrivateLink?

values.display: These service endpoints will appear as Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) with private IPs in your VPCs
values.spoken: the consumer gets network interfaces with private IPs

values.display: establishing a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to front your service
values.spoken: the provider puts an NLB in front

evidence.quote: As a service user, you will need to create interface type VPC endpoints for services that are powered by PrivateLink. These service endpoints will appear as Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) with private IPs in your VPCs.
As a service owner, you can onboard your service to AWS PrivateLink by establishing a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to front your service and create a PrivateLink service to register with the NLB.

question: Can on-premises applications use PrivateLink endpoints over Direct Connect?

values.display: The application in your on-premises can connect to the service endpoints in Amazon VPC over AWS Direct Connect

evidence.quote: Yes. The application in your on-premises can connect to the service endpoints in Amazon VPC over AWS Direct Connect.

claim: AWS PrivateLink lets you access services hosted on AWS while keeping all network traffic within the AWS network; consumers reach PrivateLink-powered services from a VPC or on premises without public IPs and without traffic crossing the internet.
question: What does AWS PrivateLink give a service consumer?

values.display: keeping all the network traffic within the AWS network
values.spoken: traffic stays on the AWS network

values.display: without using public IPs, and without requiring the traffic to traverse across the Internet

evidence.quote: AWS PrivateLink enables customers to access services hosted on AWS in a highly available and scalable manner, while keeping all the network traffic within the AWS network.

Service users can use this to privately access services powered by PrivateLink from their Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) or their on-premises, without using public IPs, and without requiring the traffic to traverse across the Internet.
